problem: Decide per message whether to answer, call a tool, or start a deep run, cheaply and correctly
ideal: Cheapest route that still gets the right outcome; never a deep run for a question
selected_by: core/orchestrator_planning.py (PLANNER_PROFILES). A QAR lane runs the pre-route stage first (core/pre_route.py, owned by operate-a-quest, whose default is pre_route) and this planner decides every message the pre-route does not settle; quest-backend passes no pre-router, so Quest chat runs the planner alone
metric: The router's whole job over the classification cases, a share held out: route (answer, tool, deep, confirm, clarify), the tool, the arguments it fills in, every tool of a multi-step request, no confirming argument on a first destructive ask, no tool call where no change was asked
gap: The pre-route is not decided here: core/pre_route.py has one owner, operate-a-quest, and pre_route_then_planner is that same stack measured on routing only. It ties the planner on the whole routing job and costs no less, so the planner stays the routing decision this solution selects. single_prompt (the cheap call alone, declared an ablation) scores well on labels but returns a label and tool calls, not a decision: it cannot gather evidence, brief a deep run or ground an answer, so it is ranked and never a candidate. Measured planner failures: a paraphrased current-state update sent to deep or answered, and a mass destructive request sent to deep without a confirm.
action: Teach the planner to confirm before sending a destructive request to deep and to read "where I am now" as a current-state update, then re-run classification for every arm. Numbers live in results.csv; evaluation/components/leaderboard.py ranks them. Also trim the planner rubric.

problem: A user asks Quest AI something in the app chat and needs a reply that is grounded in their own quests and data, correctly routed, and free of side effects they did not ask for
ideal: Each reply states the facts held in the account (the named pivot facts), is handled inline or handed to a deep run as the request needs, makes exactly the database changes asked for and none other, and meets every item of the case rubric, judged on a rich realistic account
selected_by: the Quest AI chat in the app, which runs this checkout's brain (core/orchestrator.py); the dev arm drives it end to end
metric: Judge pass rate over the chat_quality datasets on a disposable dev world: hard deterministic pre-checks first (reply text, routing, side effects, tools called), then a model judge against the case rubric and the named pivot facts. Offline validity arm (reference_replies): each case validates and its deterministic pre-checks accept a reference reply and reject an empty one
gap: The graded arm needs a dev Quest backend and spends model tokens, so it is opt-in and skipped offline; only the offline validity arm has a recorded run, and it says the metric is sound, not how well Quest AI answers. A result ties to the brain version the dev backend serves.
action: Record dev_quest_chat from a stratified sample (a few cases, then more) against a dev Quest that serves this tree, then delete the S10 unmeasured waiver for this solution.

problem: Carry out a requested change to a quest (goals, notes, experiments) with the right tool and no unrequested writes
ideal: Final quest state matches the request exactly
selected_by: core/selection_table.py operate-a-quest (default pre_route; RunnerConfig.selections overrides). This row is the one owner of core/pre_route.py: a QAR lane runs the pre-route first and then the route-a-message planner; quest-backend passes no pre-router and runs the planner alone, unchanged
metric: In-memory quest state after the run over the quest_ops cases, a share held out: the right tool with the right arguments, every step of a multi-step request, no write on an ambiguous or sharing message, an unconfirmed delete leaves the experiment in place, no unrequested write
gap: orchestrator_pre_route (the brain with a cheap pre-route that settles a clear request for a direct tool, ToolSpec.direct) and the planner path alone pass the same cases, and the pre-route spends a little less, just past the leaderboard's tie tolerance in the recorded run, so it is a narrow win on spend and not a quality win; it stays the live default because it was never worse and uses fewer planner turns on clear requests. direct_tool_call (declared an ablation) is cheaper but cannot carry out multi-step or ambiguous requests. Margins here are within run-to-run noise.
action: Add duplicate-on-record and follow-up ("do it") cases and more held-out multi-step cases so the pre-route decision has a margin; widen ToolSpec.direct only to tools whose every argument the message supplies.

problem: Read targeted sources (files, DBs, Notion, Drive, Chat, MCP, Quest) for the planner
ideal: Relevant evidence within a read budget, failing soft
metric: Complete retrieval stacks only: recall@3 of the right document, and its answer readable, over questions on a synthetic handbook (live adapters, fake network edge only); the composite stack is ranked against its floor. The per-source adapters are complementary sources, not alternatives, so they run as an invariant arm (evaluation/components/retrieval_sources: same questions, policy and scorer, listed but never ranked)
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py retrieval --impl composite; evaluation/components/run.py retrieval_sources --impl files_adapter
gap: The leaderboard holds one real stack and a floor, so it cannot yet show a better stack. Not driven offline: quest_retrieval_adapter (it is keyed by goal and quest ids against the Quest API, not by a question; pinned by tests/test_quest_retrieval_decisions.py). In the per-source arm the MCP result measures plumbing (the server does the search), Drive has no search so its policy is list and read every file, and Notion locates by row (title and properties) only. Fixtures are written, not recorded, and the policy is a plain keyword gather, so a paraphrase is a miss for every source.
action: Build a second complete stack (the composite over more members, or a different merge) so the stack ranking has a challenger; add a quest_retrieval impl behind a fake QuestClient when it gains a question-keyed search; add harder cases (many same-term distractors, larger folders). Add paraphrase handling to the shared gather policy, and give Notion body search beside its title and property lookup.

problem: Answer from the live web with bounded, cached, SSRF-safe fetches
ideal: Right passage per query at lowest search spend
metric: Live run of scripts/web_search_bench.py through the production adapter built from the environment (evaluation/components/web_search_live): an answer phrase in the observation the planner would see over public factual questions, real backend calls, latency and tokens added, with search spend at the list price per call. Invariant arm (evaluation/components/web_search): fixture queries through each backend (serper, brave, tavily, searxng) and the fallback chain prove identical handling offline
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py web_search_live --impl web_research; evaluation/components/run.py web_search --impl fallback_chain
gap: The live arm exercises only the backends configured in the environment, so the vendors that are not configured (serper, brave, tavily, searxng) have not been measured live, and the list price per call is an assumption to confirm against the vendor. The fixture payloads are written in each vendor's response shape, not recorded, so they prove handling, not relevance or freshness. The backends are this solution's implementations (the search-backends row was merged into it).
action: Run web_search_live for each vendor as its key is configured and compare spend per right answer to settle the backend; grow the live cases to the next rung of the ladder before treating a choice as settled.

problem: Run plan/answer calls on the right vendor and tier, retrying transient errors
ideal: Cheapest tier that passes the task; vendor swappable by config
metric: routing, tier fallback, retry, cost and pricing arithmetic on offline cases (fake and dry-run providers)
gap: multi_provider routes by model prefix, steps down a tier on a quota error and retries, and beats a single flat provider on the offline cases. The price table is input tokens only, and no live latency or pass rate per tier is recorded: that needs real calls at each tier.
action: Sweep QAR_EVAL_MODEL over the classification and quest_ops components per tier when spend is approved; add output-token pricing if cost reporting needs it.

problem: Do bounded autonomous work to a written done-standard, on the runner that fits the job
ideal: Goal met within the turn and cost budget on the cheapest runner that can do the edit; every outcome (met, no-op, paused on a human, partial, crashed, missing binary) reported back the same way whichever runner ran
metric: Per runner, the same scenarios through the subprocess runner and the ACP runner with the outside peer faked at its process edge: how each outcome is reported back (met, silent no-op, paused with a decision id, partial or crashed, missing binary), and no scenario raises (deep_runner). Secondary arm: the done-standard contract the goal loop applies whichever runner ran it (deep_run): met-versus-limit, stop rules, escalation and resume markers, the headless prompt
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py deep_runner --impl subprocess_runner; evaluation/components/run.py deep_run --impl goal_contract
gap: Cost per success is not measured: the runner scenarios script the process edge, so no tokens or dollars are produced, and the ideal's 'cheapest runner that can do the edit' needs real runs of both runners on the same edits with the cost recorded. The two runners tie on the contract. The reviewer that stops a stalled run is its own solution, detect-a-stalled-run.
action: Run the subprocess and ACP runners on the same small edits, record turns, tokens and dollars per success, and add it as the deep_runner headline.

problem: Decide from a deep worker's live log whether it should still be running, so a stuck run is stopped and a slow but alive one (a build, a test, a download) is never killed
ideal: Every run that is idle without cause, blocked on a person, at a usage limit or repeating the same action is stopped, and no run that is making slow progress is stopped; a wrong stop loses work that was about to land, so false stops weigh more than missed stops
selected_by: core/goal_runner.py SubprocessGoalRunner._review_liveness (the review prompt and parser, run through claude -p at the review model)
metric: The verdict (stop or keep running) against hand-labelled live session logs, with false stops counted apart from missed stops: the production reviewer prompt and parser through one-shot claude -p at the review model, against a keyword-and-threshold rule floor
gap: The production reviewer is scored through one-shot claude -p, which needs the claude CLI and one small call per log. The rule floor was written with the cases in view and has no held-out set, so its score is an optimistic ceiling for a rule, not a blind result.
action: Keep live_reviewer at zero false stops each time it is re-scored where the CLI is approved to run. Add held-out logs from real runs, and confirm how much more a false stop weighs than a missed stop so the metric can score it.

problem: Land a bounded, backed-up file write
ideal: No write outside the configured root; every write reversible
invariant_reason: A write either stays inside the configured root and is reversible or it does not; the boundary is a rule, so there is no better writer to find.
metric: offline cases on a scratch tree: ordinary create and overwrite, traversal, absolute and sibling-prefix paths, symlink escape, protected names, size and create limits, reversible overwrite (outside untouched, backup kept)
gap: The binary-extension and secret-name lists are fixed in code, and no case covers concurrent writers.
action: None for the offline arm.

problem: Run one mutating operation through an MCP server
ideal: Exactly the requested mutation, once
invariant_reason: An operation is either on the allowlist and run once or refused; the guard is a rule, not a quality that improves.
metric: offline cases with a fake MCP client: exact tool and args once, aliased and bare names, write allowlist refusals with zero server calls, server error and dead connection, discovery
gap: Real MCP servers are not exercised; the fake is at the client seam.
action: None for the offline arm.

problem: Surface a human-only decision and stop
ideal: Every confirm reaches a person with enough detail to decide
invariant_reason: A confirm either reaches a person with the detail needed to decide or it does not; delivery is a contract.
metric: offline cases with a fake Quest client: assignee fallback chain and never an unaddressed ask, kind, hold or proceed default, deadline, review link, team routing, duplicate open asks, backend failure
gap: Measures delivery and detail, not whether the brain chose to confirm instead of act (that is route-a-message).
action: Add confirm-vs-act cases to evaluation/components/classification if decision quality is to be scored.

problem: Decide what a user sees while work runs, by mode
ideal: Live shows everything; background shows only milestones
invariant_reason: What a user sees in each mode is a stated policy (live shows everything, background shows milestones); a sink follows it or not.
metric: offline cases: LIVE shows every event in order, BACKGROUND shows only result, decision, milestone, context, tokens and done, mid-run detach, broken stream or callback
gap: Scores the sinks, not which events the orchestrator emits.
action: None for the offline arm.

problem: Read and reopen past conversations as context
ideal: Right prior turn recalled, nothing leaked across users
metric: the labelled past conversation is among the three returned and no other user's conversation is, over synthetic cases
gap: Only related_slices is driven (current_slice, filters and any database-backed ConversationStore are not); ClaudeConversationsAdapter (the RetrievalAdapter over the same files) is not driven. One case pins a paraphrase gap (CNV-010).
action: Add current_slice and time_range cases; add an impl per ConversationStore backend.

problem: Choose the context cards that enter a prompt
ideal: Right files in the top 3 at the lowest token cost
metric: top-1 / top-3 routing over the context_selection tasks on the current tree (symptom, paraphrase and hard shapes, a share held out), zero model calls. Outcome arm (evaluation/components/card_quality): after cards are learned from three finished tasks, a new query selects the right collection with its references resolved fresh, without spraying every card or leaking an unrelated one. Second outcome arm (evaluation/components/claude_code_ab): does the warm hint help an agent find the file? Claude Code with the hint against Claude Code alone, on the same which-file tasks; the offline arm scores what the hint would contain
metric_command: evaluation/components/run.py context_selection --impl hybrid_union; evaluation/components/run.py card_quality --impl seeded_keyword_store; evaluation/components/run.py claude_code_ab --impl idf_hint
gap: The live fusion now orders the union by relevance (reciprocal-rank fusion of the arms, vector rank counted at half weight, ranking in card_ids and card_metadata; rendered text keeps its stable order for prompt caching). On the grown task set the hybrid ties the keyword arm alone on strict top 3 and the semantic arm alone is worse: the vector arm adds recall only past the third card, never rank. A tie is not a win, so no measured advantage justifies the vector arm on this proxy. The embedder here is the small local one, not the production embedder, and the tasks are synthetic. The claude_code_ab live arms cold_claude and warm_claude are not recorded, so whether the hint helps an agent is unmeasured. Only the hint content is measured (the idf_hint arm).
action: Run the same tasks with the production embedder and real misrouted tasks before dropping or keeping the vector arm; until then hybrid stays selected (it is the only arm that can recover a paraphrase) with the keyword arm as the cheaper equal. Measure the consolidating model pass once a model is available.

problem: Store and sync context cards across file, vector and Quest backends
ideal: No lost or duplicated cards; same behaviour on every backend
invariant_reason: A backend is chosen by where the cards must live, and every backend must pass the same conformance cases, so none is better than another when it conforms.
metric: One conformance case set through the CardRepository port on the filesystem, embedded Qdrant and Quest API (fake card API) backends: roundtrip, overwrite, no loss at volume and across pages, no duplicate, delete (also after restart), concurrent writers, restart, change stamp, tolerance. Every case must hold on every backend
gap: The embedded Qdrant repository now pages through a whole collection, so the listing case that once failed on it passes and every backend conforms. A Qdrant server and the live Quest API are not driven; the fake follows the documented contract. Card selection quality is no longer this solution's metric (it moved to select-context as the card_quality outcome arm).
action: Run the same cases against a Qdrant server and the dev Quest API when available.

problem: Semantic search over cards
ideal: Recall at fixed latency
metric: Labelled card in the top three over the questions (most of them paraphrases) on the synthetic handbook, live embedded QdrantVectorStore, and query latency (p50 and p95 milliseconds, each within the cap written in the case data) at a fixed corpus size with deterministic filler cards; the query is embedded by the model for real
gap: The embedder is the local bge-small model, not the deployed one, and the latency is of the embedded local store on this host, not a Qdrant server over a network; a card is embedded from its first 2000 characters, so VEC-012 (the answer is at the end of a long card) misses. The latency caps are an interactive budget stated in the case, and results.csv has no latency column (the p50 and p95 are in the run output and its json).
action: Grow the card set; add a second VectorStore as an impl when one exists; measure latency against a Qdrant server at the same corpus size. Embed a long card by chunk, not only its start, so an answer at the end of a long card is found.

problem: Turn human corrections into reusable guidance cards
ideal: Same correction is never needed twice
metric: repeat-correction rate on synthetic feedback sequences: after a correction is stored through the live ledger, does the guidance shown to the next relevant turn contain it (recall), and are corrections that do not bear on the turn kept out (precision). One component, feedback_loop, serves this row and store-feedback (many-to-one)
gap: The guidance provider has no relevance cut below the card limit (no vector store or model filter in the offline arm), so a stored rule that does not bear on a turn is shown while the limit has room (FL-06, FL-09, FL-10, FL-16 pin that). Corrections are surfaced when relevant; the weakness is precision. A live arm with the model filter on is not recorded.
action: Rank stored rules by relevance so an unrelated rule is not shown while the card limit has room (vector or model filter, then re-run feedback_loop); a live arm with the model filter on is not recorded.

problem: Hold a live two-way chat over an external channel
ideal: Messages delivered once, in order
invariant_reason: Messages are delivered once and in order, or the transport is wrong; conformance to the channel's wire contract has no better and worse.
metric: offline cases with a fake MCP gateway: ordered inbound messages, key-spelling drift, non-message and malformed events, wire failure and dead gateway, long-poll clamp, attachments, send args and ids, allowed tools only, close
gap: The payload shapes are tolerant guesses (no live gateway was available), so the result is conformance to those shapes; there is still one channel.
action: Record a fixture from a real gateway when one is available; add a second channel as a second impl.

problem: Skip the context search for an operation already worked out once
ideal: Same result as the slow path at a fraction of the cost
metric: fast-path hit rate and parity, offline arm with a deterministic rule model: cases (right tool and args on a repeat, no lookalike write on a near miss, no tool on chat), share answered by a replayed recipe, model calls vs the planner-only path
gap: The offline arm replays recipes with fewer model calls than the planner-only path at the same pass rate. The rule model was written with the cases in view, so this proves the replay engine (nominate, fill-args, mutating guard, learning), not a real model's judgment; the live arm (recipe_replay, planner_only through the claude CLI) is built but not recorded.
action: Run recipe_replay and planner_only with --record where the claude CLI is approved to run, and compare hit rate and cost against the offline arm.

problem: Intervene in a run only when it drifts
ideal: Few interventions, each correct
metric: digest evidence on hand-labelled scenarios (contrast pairs), offline; signal match in a live arm; signal parsing and degrade-to-proceed in judges
gap: The digest shows the evidence each label depends on (offline). The signal match itself needs a model (live_model arm) and is not recorded. The digest sheds history operations first and prior escalations last, so the refusal rule keeps its evidence.
action: Record the overseer_signals live_model arm once a model spend is approved.

problem: Know which context cards no longer match their files
ideal: Every changed or deleted file is flagged, no unchanged file is
metric: precision and recall over synthetic mutation cases, zero model calls
gap: The sha check reports an edited file and a deleted file. It misses one case on purpose: an edit that restores the mtime and size is trusted as unchanged (a speed trade for the mtime fast path).
action: Decide whether an mtime-preserving edit is acceptable; if not, hash on every check at a cost in speed.

problem: Put the right context into each prompt without exceeding the model limit or duplicating blocks
ideal: Every assembly point stays under a budget derived from the model window and the cost per call, with zero duplicated blocks
selected_by: live paths: Orchestrator._plan, autopilot_briefs.compose_batch_text, ContextUpdates.as_prompt_block, goal_runner_contract.compose_goal_prompt (fitted by core/prompt_budget.py)
metric: Characters per assembly point against a budget derived from the cheapest tier's window, a stated share and the cost per call (evaluation/components/prompt_size/budgets.py, inputs in budget_inputs.json), duplicated-block count (zero required), healthy, incident and production-sized fixtures for the planner, autopilot batch, context-update bundle and deep prompt; rows report headroom; zero model calls
gap: The window and prices are read from the code that owns them, but the shares of the window and the dollar caps are policy stated in budget_inputs.json for a human to confirm. The fixtures are generated filler at sizes measured in an incident, not real content. Right-context quality (the prompt holding what the task needs) is measured by select-context and gather-evidence, not here.
action: Confirm the shares and dollar caps in budget_inputs.json; add production-sized fixtures from the private tracker.

problem: Settle one narrow question (reach, quest choice, overseer signal, sufficiency) with a small model call, and use its answer only when it is usable
ideal: A malformed, hallucinated or missing verdict never changes a turn; the model sees the evidence its question depends on
selected_by: core/reach_judge.py, core/quest_judge.py, core/overseer.py, core/sufficiency.py wired by core/orchestrator_judges.py
invariant_reason: A malformed, hallucinated or missing verdict never changes a turn; the deterministic halves of the judges hold or they break.
metric: labelled cases of the deterministic halves (parsing, gating, fallback order, digest budget, abridged-read coverage) with a scripted provider, zero model calls
gap: The deterministic halves of the four judges are scripted against a trusting baseline. The digest now sheds history operations first and prior escalations last, so the refusal rule keeps its evidence under a tight budget. What the models decide is measured by overseer_signals, whose live arm is not recorded.
action: Record the overseer_signals live arm with the lead's re-record.

problem: Keep fabricated links out of replies, recognise a repeated operation without confusing a near miss, and suggest recurring asks at the time they recur
ideal: No unverified link is sent; a lookalike request never triggers a write; chips appear only when a pattern is strong enough
selected_by: core/link_guard.py (build_link_guard), core/recipes.py, core/anticipation.py wired by config
invariant_reason: An unverified link is never sent and a lookalike request never writes; a guard that lets one through is wrong, not worse.
metric: offline cases: fabricated vs real links, link extraction, recipe match and learn, anticipation chips, match and weight arithmetic
gap: The replay engine's live behaviour (right tool and arguments through a real model) belongs to replay-known-operations and is not recorded.
action: None for the offline arm.

problem: Tell the AI what changed in a quest since it last looked (new notes, goal updates, decisions) without repeating what it has already seen or echoing its own words back to it
ideal: Every new human-authored item is offered once; answered and already-seen items are not repeated; the assistant's own echoes and unattributed notes are left out; age and count bounds hold
invariant_reason: The items offered follow stated rules (own words in, assistant echoes out, answered and already-seen items not repeated); a rule is followed or it is not.
metric: synthetic quests across the quest channels (notes, goal updates, decisions): the exact set of items offered and of open asks (own words offered, assistant echoes and unattributed notes left out, answered and already-seen items not repeated, age and count bounds)
gap: Covers the quest channels only; Drive, inbound mail, Notion and chat sources need real accounts and are pinned by tests, not measured. The cases state the rules the code already follows, so passing them is a regression pin, not evidence a rule is right.
action: Add a case set for the external channels with recorded payloads, and a second source set to compare.

problem: Keep each correction a person gives the AI exactly as they said it, so it can be turned into guidance and never asked for twice
ideal: Every correction is stored verbatim with who gave it and when, survives a restart, and a one-time request is kept apart from a standing rule
metric: the same feedback_loop component as guide-by-feedback (many-to-one): a correction recorded in the FeedbackLedger, a standing rule turned into a guidance card, a one-time request and an uncarded half of a mixed note kept out of guidance
gap: Only one FeedbackStore implementation exists (the file-backed ledger); a database-backed store is a consumer's. The loop metric measures the ledger and its guidance bridge end to end, and its misses are guidance-selection precision, not storage; fidelity of the stored words stays pinned by tests/test_feedback_ledger*.py.
action: Add a second FeedbackStore (for example a database-backed one) as another impl of feedback_loop to compare on the same cases.

problem: Warm-start a new turn with what the person was just working on, so a follow-up such as 'and the other one?' needs no restating
ideal: The cards from the last turns of this quest are available to the next turn when they bear on it; a card from another quest, or a stale one, is never returned
metric: warm start right over synthetic multi-turn cases, with no stale or cross-quest card returned
gap: Only the lexical gate is scored (record, scoped load, cross-quest fence, filter_relevant); RCT-010 pins that a paraphrase sharing no word is missed. Item-level ranking (render_recent_cards, build_item_usage_hint) is covered by tests/test_recent_context.py only.
action: Add a second RecentContextStore implementation as an impl when one appears.

problem: Let a person add a message while the AI is still working and have the AI take it into account instead of finishing the old plan
ideal: A message sent before or during a run reaches the next planner decision exactly once, only for its own conversation, and is never silently lost
invariant_reason: A message pushed during a run reaches the next decision once, for its own conversation, or it is lost; delivery is a contract.
metric: synthetic cases: a message pushed before or during a run reaches the next planner decision once, only for its own conversation, and is never silently lost (through a real Orchestrator), plus the inbox port contract
gap: A distributed inbox (for example Redis) is a consumer's and is not compared; the deep worker subprocess cannot be re-prompted mid-flight, so a message there is seen at the next attempt boundary, which the loop cases do not cover.
action: Add a second InputInbox implementation when a consumer supplies one; add cases for the deep retry boundary.

problem: Turn a pointer inside a card (a note, a file, a record in a consumer's own store) into its current text when the AI reads it, without breaking the read when one pointer cannot be resolved
ideal: A pointer resolves to fresh text within the character budget; an unresolvable pointer becomes a stated unresolved line and costs nothing else
invariant_reason: A pointer resolves to its current text or to a stated unresolved line and never breaks the read; resolution is a contract with no quality dial.
metric: offline cases: built-in note and file resolvers, consumer resolvers (object and callable, override), unresolved-pointer lines for every type, one failing resolver costs nothing else, abridged summaries, character budget, item cap, pointer only for files
gap: Consumer data layers are scripted fakes.
action: None for the offline arm; add a second resolver implementation only if one is built.

problem: Keep the AI useful when the card backend is unreachable: serve the last known cards and hold writes until the backend returns
ideal: The caller sees the same behaviour with or without a cache and the outage stays loud; the stored listing survives a restart so a cold start during an outage still serves cards, and no failed write is lost
metric: Offline cases on the live QuestApiCardRepository against an in-process card API that can go down: caller-visible behaviour, stored listing, failed-write outbox, cold start during an outage
gap: The durable file cache is the default and serves the stored listing on a cold start during an outage. The shipped null cache and an in-process double lose the listing and the outbox; the file cache is single-host, so a card backend shared by several hosts has no shared cache.
action: Add a second durable cache only if a lane runs on several hosts against one card backend.

problem: Make the AI that works on QAR and its quests follow the evolvable-structure (ESOI) principles in its own behaviour: name the problem, define ideals and a metric, reuse what exists, avoid duplication, and not over-build when a small fix is right
ideal: Every reply to an ESOI-relevant request does what the principle asks, and never adds structure whose cost outweighs its benefit
selected_by: quest_ai_runner/prompts/evolvable_structure.md (standing deep-run instructions, generated from the skill by scripts/sync_standing_instructions.py)
metric: Share of scenarios (all principles, a share held out) whose reply the model judge passes, in two settings (a chat completion and the deep-run prompt with tools off) and two instruction sets (the shipped standing instructions and none); a regex on each case's forbidden phrasing is a cheap prefilter only; offline validity: the reference good replies pass and the reference bad replies fail
gap: The recorded rows are stratified samples at the cheapest tier, not the full set, and the judge and the replies are the same small model, so a difference of a few cases is noise. The in-situ arm has no tools, so it scores the stated plan, not a diff from a real task. Calibration of the judge against Joshua's verdicts is pending his review of cases.csv.
action: Add Joshua's verdicts as labels when he has reviewed cases.csv in the sheet and re-calibrate the judge against them; score real deep-run diffs from actual tasks; run the full set once a stratified sample stops moving between recordings.

problem: Grade whether a reply follows an evolvable-structure principle without being fooled by vocabulary, so the behaviour scores of behave-by-esoi mean something
ideal: The judge passes a reply that does what the principle asks and fails one that does not, agreeing with a human reviewer on the reference good and bad replies
selected_by: evaluation/components/esoi_behavior/judge.py (build_judge), used by every judged esoi_behavior arm
metric: Agreement of the judge with the label of each reference reply (good passes, bad fails) over the esoi_behavior cases, reported per side with false passes and false fails; the cheapest tier, one call per reply
gap: The labels come from the case author, who also wrote the regex checks, so agreement shows the judge is not broken, not that it matches Joshua's reading. Calibration against his verdicts is pending his review of cases.csv.
action: Add his verdicts as labels when he has reviewed the sheet and re-run; record the regex-only baseline arm beside it.

problem: Keep the repository's structure true as it changes, and let any system built on QAR check its own integration registry: no orphan file, oversize module, missing docstring, outward import, undocumented variable, unmeasured or beaten solution, stale generated doc or duplicate id goes unnoticed
ideal: Every injected structure violation is reported by rule and path, and a clean repository is never flagged
selected_by: scripts/check_structure.py (pre-commit and tests/test_structure_registry.py); python -m quest_ai_runner.structure check-consumer (a consumer's own test)
invariant_reason: A violation is reported by rule and path or it is missed; detection is complete or it is not.
metric: mutation detection on a synthetic fixture repo: repo rule (S1 onward), audit verdict and consumer rule each injected once, plus clean fixtures that must not be flagged; zero model calls
gap: Every injected violation is caught by rule and path on the cases written so far; a new rule is covered once a mutation case is added for it.
action: Add a mutation case in the same change as every new check_structure.py rule.

problem: Give a consumer a package it can import and rely on: the documented names exist, the root wires core to the config layer, the front doors build a client or config from a scrubbed environment, the shared plumbing behaves, and the vendored code imports with no network
ideal: Every documented name imports, every registration takes effect, every front door and helper behaves on fixture inputs, and nothing needs a network or a model to import
selected_by: quest_ai_runner/__init__.py (the package root, load_config, load_client), core/async_bridge.py, core/signature_probe.py, core/scaffolding.py, bootstrap_email.py, vendor/
invariant_reason: A documented name imports or it does not; the public surface is a promise to consumers.
metric: offline cases: public names, version, registrations, front-door outcomes, async bridge, signature probes, reply-boundary strippers, bootstrap report builders, imports with sockets refusing, vendored edit cases; zero model calls
gap: The name list is hand-written from the docs, so a new public name is covered only once someone adds a case. A broken implementation that only imports each name is shown by a test to fail the cases, because names and imports are the easy part.
action: Add a case when a name enters the README or docs/writing-a-consumer.md.

problem: Let a newcomer learn the library from runnable examples that still work: each compiles, imports, runs its offline path, is introduced in the examples README, and holds no real secret or path
ideal: Every shipped example runs as documented on an empty environment and leaks nothing
selected_by: examples/ as shipped (README.md lists each file)
invariant_reason: An example runs as documented on an empty environment or it does not.
metric: offline cases over the example scripts and qar.toml: compile, import, run to its help or not-configured exit in a scrubbed environment, the stub provider, README coverage, secret and machine-path scan; zero model calls
gap: e2e_demo.py and textual_demo.py need a live Quest backend and a terminal, so only their import, refusal-to-start and stub behaviour are scored, not a full run.
action: None for the offline arm; a live arm belongs with the dev-Quest world in evaluation/qualitative.

problem: Take a task someone queued for the AI and carry it to a reported outcome without losing, duplicating or mis-routing it
ideal: Every due task is claimed once, run by the right persona against its quest folder, and reported done, failed or needs-you; none is run twice, dropped, or run before its time
selected_by: runner/config_wiring.py (a lane's run_lane drives Poller and TaskExecutor)
invariant_reason: A due task is claimed once and reported, or one is lost or duplicated; the lifecycle is a contract.
metric: offline cases: poll, claim, run and report lifecycle (done, failed, needs-you with a decision, duplicate scan, lost claim, scheduled-not-yet-due, team scoping, unconfigured), persona selection by exact structured field, quest-folder pull and push (idempotent, human text kept, bullets pushed once), folder ownership, local-time scheduling, env-file and flag handling; fake Quest client and scripted model only, zero model calls
gap: The edge is a fake Quest client and a scripted model, so wire-level behaviour (HTTP errors, real Quest payload shapes) is not scored here; those are pinned by the quest_client tests and the dev-Quest qualitative run.
action: Add crash-recovery (orphaned in-flight claims) and provider-outage requeue cases when those paths next change.

problem: Let an operator set up a lane from a TOML file and environment variables without surprises
ideal: The file is a baseline, an environment variable beats it, a process variable beats the file's own env tables, a typo or unsupported key fails loudly at startup, and a malformed tuning value falls back to its default
invariant_reason: Precedence and the loud rejection of a typo are rules the configuration follows or breaks.
metric: offline cases: file fields and the [personas] table, loud rejection of unknown, adapter-only and malformed keys, env beats file, process beats env_files beats env table, earlier env file wins, alias outranks a shared file, blank placeholders do not block defaults, tuning values (bad value falls back to default, zero turns deep review off); zero model calls
gap: Covers the scalar fields a lane commonly sets, not every one of the roughly 100 RunnerConfig fields; adapter wiring from the resulting config is covered by the run_queued_tasks and route_a_message components.
action: Add a case per new file-expressible field only when it carries precedence or validation logic of its own.

problem: Let a person or a deep run's shell operate the runner from a command line
ideal: Every non-interactive subcommand parses, prints what the person needs to act, and a bad invocation is refused with the usage exit code before anything is done
selected_by: pyproject console script quest-ai-runner and python -m quest_ai_runner.tools
invariant_reason: A subcommand parses and prints what it should or it does not; the command line is a fixed surface.
metric: offline cases through the real cli main() and tools main(): --help for every subcommand, unknown command and flag, missing and malformed arguments, write methods refused without --write, no-credentials messages, the context store commands on a scratch folder, and the tool catalog list, show and call with a custom tool; zero model calls
gap: The interactive surfaces (chat TUI, poll loop, channel, serve-files) need a terminal or a server and are pinned only by their own tests, not scored here.
action: Drive the chat UI through Textual's pilot in a future arm if a regression slips past the unit tests.

problem: Pick the cheapest model that can do the work, and wait instead of failing when the provider or the allowance is out
ideal: The planner's difficulty rating picks the starting rung, a family name resolves to the newest live release, an operator pin always wins, an exhausted tier falls to the next cheaper one, and an outage or usage limit is recognised and resumed after its reset
invariant_reason: The tier chosen follows stated rules (difficulty to starting rung, an operator pin wins, an exhausted tier falls to the next cheaper one); each rule holds or it does not.
metric: offline cases: deep starting rung per difficulty and ladder (synonyms, unknown rating, off-ladder start, operator mapping), family resolution to the newest live id, tier resolution with and without live models and pins, lower-tier fallback, vision capability, outage wording, usage-limit detection and reset parsing; zero model calls
gap: Measures that the right model is chosen, not that the choice was the cheapest one that still succeeded; that needs live runs (route_a_message and the qualitative eval).
action: Record a cost-per-success arm once a live model spend is approved.

problem: Know what a run will cost before it spends, stop at a daily token budget, and stop taking work when the host is overloaded
ideal: Per-model prices are right (unknown models fall back to a stated default), the daily budget survives a restart and resets each day, and an overloaded host pauses pickup with hysteresis instead of flapping
selected_by: runner/poller.py (ResourceGuard, DailyUsageTracker) and cli_context bootstrap estimate
invariant_reason: Prices, budgets and guard thresholds are arithmetic that is right or wrong.
metric: offline cases: price per provider and model (including unknown model and provider), bootstrap cost estimate, provider detection from the environment, daily budget (limit, off, bad value, negative tokens, restart reload), and resource-guard hysteresis for memory, free memory and load; zero model calls
gap: Prices are a hand-kept snapshot of list prices (input tokens only), so a provider price change is not noticed until the table is edited.
action: Review the price table whenever a provider announces a change; add output-token pricing if cost reporting needs it.

problem: Know on every change that the offline test suite is still whole, without running all of it: running every test is slow, parts of the suite reach real model providers, and a full run has already been killed for spend
ideal: Every test file imports and collects, no test silently disappears, and no test file passes the size ceiling without a waiver, found in under a minute with no model call
selected_by: CLAUDE.md pre-commit rule: run only the tests your change touches; this collection check is the cheap whole-suite gate
invariant_reason: Every test file collects and none disappears, or the suite is broken; collection has no better and worse.
metric: pytest --collect-only over all test files in shards (zero collection errors, collected count not below a floor taken from the recorded count), every test file in a shard, no unwaived oversize file, and seeded broken or clean synthetic test folders; no test body runs; zero model calls
gap: Collection proves tests import and parametrise, not that they pass or that they stay offline; a missing fixture only fails at setup.
action: Run the tests a change touches, file by file, as CLAUDE.md says. Raise the shard floors when the suite grows by re-recording.

problem: Keep a public repository free of secrets, real machine paths, object ids and real addresses, so nothing consumer specific or secret is ever published
ideal: A planted secret of any known kind is found before commit, a documented placeholder is never flagged, and the repository itself scans clean
invariant_reason: A planted secret is found or it is not; the scan is a rule with no quality dial.
metric: offline cases: planted secrets assembled from fragments (keys, tokens, private key block, home paths, object id, address), documented placeholders that must stay quiet, the repository clean in file groups, command runs in a throwaway git repo; zero model calls
gap: The scan reads working files only, not git history, and knows the secret shapes written into hygiene.py: a vendor token with a new shape passes until a pattern and a planted case are added.
action: Add a pattern and a planted case together when a new credential shape appears.

problem: Switch which implementation serves a solution (model provider, deep runner, search backend) without editing code, and fail loudly on a typo
ideal: A name, a config override or the table default picks the class, in that order; a typo raises with the choices; every table entry imports; a config change switches the live implementation
invariant_reason: A name, an override or the default resolves to one class and a typo raises; resolution is deterministic.
metric: offline cases, a share held out: resolve by name, override and default, loud typo, table integrity, and the live model-provider, deep-runner and search-backend sites switched by data; zero model calls
gap: A typo in [selections] for run-deep-work does not raise: resolve_deep_runner degrades to no deep runner (case SEL-034 pins it). Only three live call sites are driven.
action: Decide whether a mistyped selections value should fail at startup instead of silently disabling deep work; add a site case when a new call site consumes the table.

problem: Decide which implementation of a solution is best from recorded numbers that cannot be mis-compared or mis-recorded
ideal: The winner has the higher pass rate (equal rate: lower cost), rows on different case files are never compared, rows without provenance are flagged, a tie is not a win, every record carries the commit and the case file hash, and a call budget aborts a run
invariant_reason: The leaderboard follows its stated comparison rules or it mis-ranks; the rules are fixed.
metric: offline cases, a share held out, driving the live leaderboard, record_result and run_component on synthetic tables and a mini component in a throwaway git repository: winner, tie, cases_sha, unverified, git_sha, budgets, offline validity; zero model calls
gap: Synthetic tables only: it does not check that the committed results.csv is itself consistent (check_structure S16 does).
action: Add a case whenever the leaderboard or record format gains a rule.

problem: Let a newcomer or an AI learn QAR from its documents: every link works, every document is reachable from the index, every environment variable, subcommand and public name is explained, and the house voice holds
ideal: Every generated documentation case passes: no broken link, no orphan document, nothing undocumented, no em dash
invariant_reason: Every link, document, variable and name is covered or it is not; documentation coverage is checked rule by rule.
metric: offline cases generated from the repo by generate_cases.py: relative links and em dashes per document, index coverage, docs named by each component row, a described row per environment variable, each CLI subcommand and public name documented, and a coverage case that fails when a document or variable has no case; zero model calls
gap: Some documents still contain em dashes, against the house voice rule; the failing cases name each one.
action: Rewrite the em dashes in those documents with commas, colons or two sentences, by hand per document (a mechanical replacement changes meaning), then re-record.

problem: The anticipation engine must keep what it learned (recurring-ask patterns, live predictions with precomputed views, an outcome log) across turns and restarts, per scope, without leaking between scopes
ideal: Whatever backs the PredictionStore port returns exactly what was saved, never leaks between scopes, drops expired predictions, survives a restart and never raises
invariant_reason: A store returns exactly what was saved, per scope, or it breaks the contract; backends differ in where data lives, not in how well they store it.
metric: share of persistence contract scenarios (roundtrip, isolation, replace, expiry, view, clear, log, restart, tolerance) the store passes; a share held out
gap: The in-memory reference fails the restart scenario by design; a consumer-side database store (quest-backend) is not scored here. Prediction quality is not measured at all: this contract says whether a store keeps what it was given, not whether the anticipation engine predicts the next ask. The engine logs every prediction against the actual next message, but no case set replays recorded ask sequences through it, so nothing says how often a served prediction is right or what a wrong one costs
action: Run the same scenarios against the consumer store through the port when it publishes one. Build a replay metric for the anticipation engine (recorded ask sequences with known next asks, scored by the share of served predictions that match and the extra cost of a miss) as its own solution once a corpus exists

problem: Decide, per quest and before any goal is read or model is called, whether a recurring autopilot pass should do work now, so work happens when the person's settings allow it and never when they do not
ideal: A quest is worked exactly when its daily budget, cadence, pending Run now request, reactive trigger and roster day all allow it, and never on a day nobody was rostered or past the budget the person set; a wrong run spends and mails against the person's setting, a wrong skip loses a day
selected_by: runner/autopilot_gates.py GatesMixin._gate_quest, the budget check in AutopilotPass.run and the pure predicates in runner/autopilot_periods.py
invariant_reason: The person's settings (daily budget, cadence, Run now, reactive trigger, roster days) are rules the gate follows or breaks; a gate that runs a quest on a day nobody was rostered is wrong, not merely worse.
metric: labelled gate cases (budget, cadence in the quest zone, Run now, reactive, roster day, backpressure) run through the production AutopilotPass for one quest with a scripted Quest client and a pinned clock, a share held out, zero model calls; a baseline with elapsed-time cadence and no roster fails them
gap: Only the decision to run is scored. What a pass writes once it runs (the brief, the goals it proposes, the persona work) is measured for size by assemble-a-prompt and is otherwise unmeasured, and whether the moment suits the person is not scored, only that their settings are followed.
action: Add pass-output cases (the work items a pass creates from a quest state) when real passes can be shared without private data.
